quests.instruction: Find the platform the train will now leave from.
quests.hint: Delay, time, and two platforms are all in one announcement. Listen for the contrast marker ‘rather than’.
quests.explanation: Platform two is the platform the train will not use. The delay and the ten fifteen are other details. So the answer is 6.
quests.textToSpeak: Attention, passengers on the ten fifteen to Manchester. Due to a signal failure, this service has been delayed by approximately twenty minutes. However, it will now depart from platform six rather than platform two. We apologize for the inconvenience.

quests.instruction: Listen for where photography is completely banned.
quests.hint: Some places have partial limits and one has a total ban. ‘At all’ signals the strongest rule.
quests.explanation: Correct: the special exhibition. In the other galleries, photos are allowed as long as you don't use flash.
quests.textToSpeak: Welcome to the museum. Photography is allowed in most galleries, although flash is not permitted anywhere. In the special exhibition on the second floor, no photography is allowed at all.

quests.instruction: Spot when the storm should reach the coast.
quests.hint: Two weather events happen at different times. The storm and the inland rain are not the same thing.
quests.explanation: The answer is tomorrow evening. This afternoon is only when the inland rain begins.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the weather service, the storm should reach the coast by tomorrow evening, but in the meantime we'll see heavy rain inland starting this afternoon.

quests.instruction: Notice the launch month the speaker would prefer.
quests.hint: An earlier agreement and a personal preference are contrasted. Focus on ‘I'd rather’.
quests.explanation: Correct: September. June was the agreed date, but the speaker wants more time to test.
quests.textToSpeak: I know we agreed to launch in June, but given the testing delays, I'd rather push it to September than release something buggy.

quests.instruction: Wipe the glass and tap the price the supplier finally quoted.
quests.hint: ‘Originally’ marks the old figure. The new figure comes after the change.
quests.explanation: Correct: $32,000. Forty thousand was the first quote, and the order reduction lowered it.
quests.textToSpeak: The supplier originally quoted us forty thousand, but after we reduced the order size, they dropped it to thirty-two.

quests.instruction: Listen for who will actually finish the training by the end of the month.
quests.hint: The speaker describes an ideal outcome first. Listen for what is realistic.
quests.explanation: The sales team is correct. ‘Every employee’ is the ideal. The operations team will do it after the audit.
quests.textToSpeak: Ideally, I'd have every employee complete the training by the end of the month. Realistically, though, only the sales team will manage it by then. Operations won't get to it until after the audit.

quests.instruction: Tap what the speaker did right after customer support.
quests.hint: The career is described in order. Listen for the first move.
quests.explanation: Managing is the most recent role. So the answer is training staff.
quests.textToSpeak: I started in customer support, then moved into training after about two years, and I've been managing the team for the past three.

quests.instruction: Listen for what the speaker enjoys most about the job.
quests.hint: One thing is denied, then something else is offered. Listen for the positive point.
quests.explanation: Helping new staff grow is correct. The pay is fair, but it is not the speaker's main reason for enjoying the job.
quests.textToSpeak: What I enjoy most isn't the pay, although it's fair. It's the chance to see new hires grow into confident employees.

quests.instruction: Spot why the speaker can't start earlier.
quests.hint: The reason follows ‘because’. Listen for how it links to the current job.
quests.explanation: The answer is the notice period. The speaker must give a month's notice before leaving.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not available until the first of October, because I have to give a month's notice at my current company.

quests.instruction: Listen for the share of customers who cared most about delivery speed.
quests.hint: Several numbers appear. Match the percentage to the concern.
quests.explanation: Sixty percent said price. Twelve hundred is the number of people surveyed. So the answer is 25%.
quests.textToSpeak: Our survey covered twelve hundred customers. Of those, sixty percent said price was their main concern, while twenty-five percent cared more about delivery speed.

quests.instruction: Pick out when online sales dropped.
quests.hint: The trend goes up, down, and up again. Find the dip.
quests.explanation: Correct: summer. Sales rose until spring and recovered in autumn.
quests.textToSpeak: The trend is clear: online sales rose steadily until spring, dipped over the summer, and then recovered sharply in autumn.

quests.instruction: Listen for what the company did instead of hiring more people.
quests.hint: ‘Rather than’ shows the option that was not chosen. Focus on what follows the comma.
quests.explanation: The answer is automated routine tasks. Hiring was the option the company rejected.
quests.textToSpeak: Rather than hiring more staff, the company decided to automate the routine tasks, which freed up time for the existing team.

quests.instruction: Pick out when you should press the reset button.
quests.hint: ‘Unless’ marks the single exception where an action is allowed.
quests.explanation: The answer is only if unplugging fails. The reset button is a last resort, since it erases the settings.
quests.textToSpeak: To reset the router, unplug it for thirty seconds, plug it back in, and wait until the second light turns green. Don't press the reset button unless that doesn't work, because it erases your settings.

quests.instruction: Listen for what is not sufficient on its own.
quests.hint: One document is required and another is not enough. Listen for the negative.
quests.explanation: A bank statement is correct. The original receipt is what is required.
quests.textToSpeak: You can claim the expense within ninety days, but you'll need the original receipt. A bank statement isn't enough on its own.

quests.instruction: Spot what to do if you only have fresh bread.
quests.hint: The best case is described first. The backup is introduced with ‘if’.
quests.explanation: Ten minutes in the oven makes fresh bread act like day-old bread. So the answer is dry it in the oven.
quests.textToSpeak: The recipe works best with day-old bread, because fresh bread turns soggy. If you only have fresh, dry it in the oven for ten minutes first.

quests.instruction: Listen for the drawback of the cheaper hotel.
quests.hint: Two speakers disagree. One raises a problem, and the other answers it.
quests.explanation: It's far from the venue is correct. The first speaker mentions the forty-minute distance as an objection.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd go with the cheaper hotel. But it's forty minutes from the venue. True, but we'd save enough for a taxi each day. Fine, if you've done the math.

quests.instruction: Spot how many runners took part this year.
quests.hint: This year and last year are compared. Choose the smaller number.
quests.explanation: The answer is about 9,000. Last year had about a thousand more runners.
quests.textToSpeak: Despite the heavy rain, the marathon went ahead, and nearly nine thousand runners took part, about a thousand fewer than last year.

quests.instruction: Listen for when the flight finally left.
quests.hint: Two rebookings happen. ‘In the end’ points to the last one.
quests.explanation: The next morning is correct. The evening flight was the first rebooking.
quests.textToSpeak: My flight was rebooked twice: first to the evening, then to the following morning. So in the end I landed almost a full day late.

quests.instruction: Identify what the client must accept for the project to go ahead.
quests.hint: The word ‘unless’ names the condition that avoids the negative result.
quests.explanation: Without it, the company will decline. So the answer is a smaller scope.
quests.textToSpeak: They're asking for a lot more than we budgeted, so unless the client accepts a smaller scope, we'll have to decline the project.

quests.instruction: Listen for what was combined after the merger.
quests.hint: Some things stayed separate and one thing merged. Notice ‘but’.
quests.explanation: The finance departments is correct. The offices stayed apart.
quests.textToSpeak: After the merger, the two companies kept their separate offices, but the finance departments were combined into one team based in Dublin.

quests.instruction: Pick out what the event turned out to be.
quests.hint: Expectation and reality are different. ‘Turned out’ signals reality.
quests.explanation: A workshop is correct. The speaker expected a lecture, but it is an interactive session.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd expected a lecture, but it turned out to be more of a workshop, so bring something to write on.

quests.instruction: Notice where the speaker actually went.
quests.hint: The first shop wasn't an option. The speaker moved on to another one.
quests.explanation: The answer is the shop on Main. Elm Street's shop has closed.
quests.textToSpeak: Apparently the shop on Elm Street closed last month, so I went to the one on Main, which doesn't stock the item either.

quests.instruction: Find the average commute.
quests.hint: One number is an average and another is a distance for a group of people.
quests.explanation: 40 minutes is correct. Twenty minutes is only the walk to the station.
quests.textToSpeak: The average commute here is about forty minutes, but many people live within a twenty-minute walk of the station, so they don't count.

quests.instruction: Focus on what the committee removed.
quests.hint: ‘Not before’ links approval to a change. What changed?
quests.explanation: The committee approved the plan after removing it. So the answer is the parking garage.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee eventually approved the plan, though not before removing the parking garage, which was the most controversial part.

quests.instruction: Tap what she does when the weather is bad.
quests.hint: The old habit and the new habits are different. The weather decides which new habit.
quests.explanation: Correct: takes the bus. She cycles in decent weather and takes the bus otherwise.
quests.textToSpeak: She used to take the underground, but since the fares went up she cycles when the weather's decent, and takes the bus when it isn't.

quests.instruction: Listen for when the author received feedback.
quests.hint: ‘A week after that’ counts from the last date mentioned.
quests.explanation: The editor finished on the tenth, and feedback came seven days after that. So the answer is the 17th.
quests.textToSpeak: The manuscript arrived on the third, the editor finished reading it on the tenth, and the author received feedback a week after that.

quests.instruction: Tap how many topics remain for the next session.
quests.hint: The plan, what was done, and what remains are all numbers. Find the leftover.
quests.explanation: The answer is 4. Ten planned, six covered, and four remaining.
quests.textToSpeak: We were hoping to cover ten topics, but we only had time for six, so we'll cover the remaining four next session.

quests.instruction: Listen for who won the award.
quests.hint: Two people are mentioned with hours. The award goes to the higher number.
quests.explanation: Marisol is correct. Ken came close but did not have the most hours.
quests.textToSpeak: The award goes to the volunteer who has given the most hours over the past year. This year, that's Marisol, with over four hundred hours, although Ken came close with three hundred and eighty.

quests.instruction: Clear the glass and tap how much notice is needed for leave during the holidays.
quests.hint: There is a normal rule and a special rule. Choose the special one.
quests.explanation: Two weeks is the regular notice period. So the answer is one month.
quests.textToSpeak: Under the new policy, employees need to request leave two weeks ahead, but during the holidays they need to give a full month's notice.

quests.instruction: Listen for what happened by the second weekend.
quests.hint: The situation changes over time. Follow the chain from opening night.
quests.explanation: Every show sold out is correct. It is the result of people recommending the play.
quests.textToSpeak: The theater was half empty on opening night, but word of mouth spread quickly, and by the second weekend every show was sold out.
